one_liner: Distributed MPI+CUDA sparse LU direct solver using regular 2D sparse blocks; reports up to 11.7-18x over SuperLU_DIST on 128 GPUs.
what_it_does: Solves square sparse systems Ax = b by LU factorization on CPU or multi-GPU clusters. The C API has five calls: pangulu_init (rank 0 passes the whole CSC matrix and the library reorders and distributes it), pangulu_gstrf (factor), pangulu_gstrs (solve one right-hand side in place, repeatable), pangulu_gssv (both) and pangulu_finalize. It is not a drop-in for SuperLU_DIST: inputs, options and the process-grid setup differ, and the value type (real or complex, single or double) is fixed at compile time by a -DCALCULATE_TYPE_* flag.
how_it_is_fast: Instead of supernodal or multifrontal layouts, the matrix is cut into equal nb x nb blocks that stay sparse, which avoids the extra fill a dense supernode stores, and the blocks are mapped 2D block-cyclically over a p x q process grid. Each block task (GETRF, TSTRF, GESSM, SSSSM) adaptively picks a sparse or dense BLAS kernel on CPU or GPU, and a synchronisation-free communication scheme lets ranks start tasks as soon as their inputs arrive instead of waiting at level barriers. Version 5.0 adds a task aggregator for numeric factorization and a smaller GPU memory layout.
when_to_use: Large unsymmetric sparse systems whose factors outgrow one node, on an MPI cluster with one NVIDIA GPU per rank, where you would otherwise run SuperLU_DIST

Matrices whose factors are still fairly sparse inside blocks, so sparse block kernels beat SuperLU_DIST's dense supernodal kernels (an independent 2025 study on one A100 found PanguLU about 2.2x faster than SuperLU_DIST in numeric factorization, geometric mean, derived from its abstract)
Many right-hand sides with a fixed matrix: factor once with pangulu_gstrf, then call pangulu_gstrs repeatedly
Complex-valued or single-precision systems on GPUs (all four value types are supported, chosen at build time)
when_not_to_use: Ill-conditioned or hard-to-pivot matrices: numeric factorization does no partial pivoting and silently replaces pivots smaller than 1e-16 with 1e-16, MC64 static pivoting is optional and unavailable for complex values, and there is no iterative refinement; open issue #5 (2025, unanswered) reports relative residuals around 10 for some matrices and kernels
Single-GPU use where newer solvers exist: Caracal (SC25) reports up to 94x over PanguLU on one A100, and the structure-aware irregular blocking paper reports 1.50x over PanguLU

Reproducing the paper's numbers out of the box: closed issue #2 measured 2-10x slower factorization than the paper on one A100 40GB (cage12: 578.7 s numeric, 7.3 GFLOP/s) with no maintainer explanation
Proprietary or SaaS products that cannot accept AGPL-3.0, which also covers network use
AMD GPUs with the current code: the SC'23 paper ran on MI50, but the repo ships only CPU and CUDA platform backends

integration.dependencies: MPI (tested MPICH 4.3.0), OpenMP, BLAS for CPU kernels (tested OpenBLAS 0.3.26), CUDA for GPU (tested 12.9), optional METIS (32-bit index build); MC64 is built in
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler with OpenMP (gcc), mpicc, nvcc and GNU make; you edit make.inc and examples/Makefile by hand (it builds both libpangulu.a and libpangulu.so)
integration.platforms: Linux clusters, x86-64 CPU-only or NVIDIA GPU; make.inc defaults to -gencode arch=compute_61 (Pascal), so edit it for newer GPUs such as the A100 (sm_80)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the library keeps some settings in global variables and the example initialises MPI with MPI_THREAD_MULTIPLE, so treat one solver per process at a time as the safe pattern

gotchas: On errors such as a null options pointer, nb = 0 or a value-type mismatch, the library calls exit(1) inside the solver rather than returning a status
The process grid is p x q, where p is the largest divisor of the rank count at or below its square root, so a prime number of ranks gives a 1 x P grid
Missing structural diagonal entries are filled with 1e-8 before factoring, which perturbs the matrix you passed in
Block size nb strongly affects speed and must be tuned per matrix (the example uses -nb 10 on a toy matrix; init falls back to 256 only when nb is negative)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick PanguLU over CKTSO, GSS or RSLAB when you need a distributed, multi-node GPU LU and SuperLU_DIST is your reference. For single-node circuit matrices CKTSO targets KLU-class workloads, and for SPD systems a Cholesky solver such as BaSpaCho or the task-based CHOLMOD is the better fit.
verified_claims_summary: Per the SC'23 paper's abstract (paper body not opened, so matrices, SuperLU_DIST version and flags are unknown), PanguLU reached up to 11.70x over SuperLU_DIST on 128 NVIDIA A100s and up to 17.97x on 128 AMD MI50s, and scaled 47.51x and 74.84x over one GPU. These are best-case maxima from the 2023 code, not typical ratios. An independent 2025 paper (Hu et al.) implies about 2.2x over SuperLU_DIST on one A100 (derived from the 1.50x and 3.32x geometric means in its abstract).
status_note: Active research code (v5.0.0, latest commit 2026-06-25, 38 commits, 51 stars), but AGPL-3.0, with an unanswered accuracy report (issue #5) and an unanswered performance-gap report (issue #2), so validate residuals on your own matrices before adopting it.
